A Watch at Dusk

Miriam Vale

The last entry was never finished.
I kept the bakery open for the names on his list. At dusk we sat together. The ticking passed our window and went on down the road.
In that round room, one glass case shone before his hand moved. I threw my pan at the shining glass. For a moment he was the one afraid.

Glass That Fed It

Elias Venn

The last entry was never finished.
Three skulls. Four blocks of soul sand. We expected a monster. Its own ribs swallowed it and left a doorway. We should have left then.
The doorway inside was still there. I crawled back through it. The others kept shooting from the shelter; the thing did not even flinch.

The Eye That Waited

Nessa Ward

The last entry was never finished.
Twelve eyes, no doorway. I stood on the frame and reached into the dark with my gift. It was like holding a breath through my hands. It took everything.
One eye kept my light while I rested. Not long. I stood on the eye beside it, on the same straight edge, and tried again. The two lights found each other.

Under a Violet Sky

Owen Pike

The last entry was never finished.
We followed the beam down from the dragon's crystal to a glass focus. There was a plate to stand on. My gift answered when I faced the glass and held it there.
When the feed broke, the dragon came down. That was our chance. The low wave could be jumped. Its long lines stayed where they first appeared; we moved sideways.

Nine Quiet Footsteps

Arun Bellamy

The last entry was never finished.
The grey coat walked beside the prisoner. Wherever he went, my sparks died. Hiding behind a wall did nothing. Backing away let them return.
We drew the others off. I stayed beyond his quiet and struck the grey coat first. The prisoner's hands lit before the man reached the ground.
